docs.title: Theory
docs.text: UNDER CONSTRUCTION

docs.title: Chrono coupling
docs.text:
Under review by Iván Martínez Estévez

XML configuration, collision models and mechanical constraints in DualSPHysics v6.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
The coupling connects DualSPHysics rigid bodies to Project Chrono for contact modelling and mechanical links. Contact modelling controls how bodies collide; links impose connections or apply spring and damping forces. These are separate parts of the XML configuration. The six mechanisms covered here are linear springs, Coulomb damping, sliding joints, spherical joints, hinges and pulleys. They represent the subset described by the original XML Guide, rather than the complete capabilities of Project Chrono.

For coupling theory, see Coupling DualSPHysics with Project Chrono. This page concentrates on configuring the XML.

The XML excerpts below require the surrounding case definitions, geometry, bodies and parameters indicated by their XML locations. Reference-format options are identified separately.

docs.title: Coupling architecture and model selection
docs.text:
DualSPHysics discretises the fluid and boundary geometry into particles, evaluates the fluid dynamics and computes fluid–solid interaction. DSPHChronoLib provides the communication layer between DualSPHysics and Project Chrono. Chrono solves the configured mechanical constraints and solid–solid contacts; its FEA module supplies the structural response when ChronoFEA bodies are present.

For a rigid floating body, DualSPHysics transfers the interaction-derived linear and angular input to the library and obtains the updated centre, linear velocity and angular velocity. The coupling then updates the particle boundary. A mechanical constraint restricts or loads the connected bodies; a contact model resolves collisions. These responsibilities remain distinct even when both act on the same body.

Figure 10: DualSPHysics, DSPHChronoLib and Project Chrono exchange information through the coupling interface.

A rigid body retains its shape. A ChronoFEA beam instead has structural nodes and section properties, with a particle representation reconstructed from its deforming beam mesh. The separate TL-SPH Flexible Structures model computes solid dynamics within DualSPHysics using structural particles. Their material definitions and mechanical constraints are not interchangeable.

The selected installation must supply compatible libraries, including FEA support where needed. Upstream Project Chrono capabilities and workshop compilation recipes do not, by themselves, establish that a particular element or actuator is exposed by the current DualSPHysics XML interface.

docs.title: Activating Chrono
docs.text:
The current v6 parameter uses CHR to select Chrono for rigid-body collisions. Place it inside case/execution/parameters:

XML excerpt — activation. XML location: case/execution/parameters. Source: examples/chrono/07_DamBreakCubes/DamBreak1Cube_Def.xml.

<parameter key="RigidAlgorithm" value="CHR" comment="Rigid Algorithm: FREE:collision-free, SPH, DEM, CHR:Chrono collision (default=SPH)"/>

The v6 choices are FREE (collision-free), SPH, DEM and CHR; the documented default is SPH. The presentation's numeric 3 is still accepted by the reader but emits a deprecation warning. Use the named v6 value in new documentation.

The mechanical configuration belongs separately under case/execution/special/chrono. A present chrono section causes the reader to initialise the coupling, subject to Chrono library availability. Do not treat CHR as a universal prerequisite for every link-only configuration: the current examples/chrono/01_Pendulum/CasePendulum_Def.xml uses FREE with spherical links. Conversely, selecting CHR while collisions are disabled produces a warning. Retain the intended collision model of the complete source case.

docs.title: General settings and body declarations
docs.text:
These sibling elements are extracted from the spring point-absorber case. Their parent is its existing chrono element; the complete spring section is shown below under Linear spring.

XML excerpt — general-settings. XML location: case/execution/special/chrono. Source: examples/chrono/10_PointAbsorber/CasePointAbsorberSpring_Def.xml.

<savedata value="0.05" comment="Saves CSV with data exchange for each time interval (0=all steps)"/>
<schemescale value="1" comment="Scale used to create the initial scheme of Chrono objects (default=1)"/>
<bodyfixed id="Bottom" mkbound="0"/>
<bodyfloating id="Floater" mkbound="50"/>
Element or attribute Meaning Units / context savedata/@value CSV exchange-data interval; 0 requests every step; the reader default -1 disables these periodic files s for positive intervals schemescale/@value Scale for the initial Chrono scheme; also used in spring visualisation sizing Dimensionless; default 1 bodyfixed Existing fixed boundary associated with a Chrono body id names the body referenced by links; mkbound identifies the boundary bodyfloating Existing floating boundary associated with a Chrono body Physical mass, inertia and degrees of freedom remain part of the case bodymoving Moving boundary declaration supported by the current format; includes massbody Use the relevant complete moving-body case idbody1, idbody2 References to declared Chrono body IDs A missing idbody2 connects the applicable link to the world

Body names are case-sensitive references. A range such as id="arm" mkbound="0-3" creates arm0, arm1, arm2 and arm3; it does not create one body named arm. The mkbound value is a boundary identifier, not the full particle mk value.

An underscore-prefixed entry such as _savedata is inactive. Several current cases retain such entries, so their displayed values must not be described as enabled output settings.

docs.title: Output files and additional v6 controls
docs.text:
The implementation still writes CfgChrono_Scheme.vtk, ChronoBody_forces.csv and ChronoExchange_mkbound_<number>.csv. Names containing a boundary number depend on the configured bodies. Spring representations use SpringVtk/Chrono_Springs_<sequence>.vtk; collision geometry is generated under chrono_objs/. These paths are relative to the configured simulation output directory, whose name need not be Case_out.

ChronoExchange_mkbound_<number>.csv records linear acceleration inputs in m/s², angular acceleration inputs in rad/s² and returned body kinematics. These acceleration columns are not forces in newtons. Body and link force outputs are separate products; confirm their load contributions, coordinate frames and moment references before interpreting a resultant as an impact-force measure.

The current format also documents gravity (default true), ompthreads (default 1) and optional timestepper/substepping. Substepping has off, fixed and auto modes, with maxdt, maxsteps, maxdispdp and maxrot controls. These are additional v6 reference options, not changes to apply automatically to the source cases. Choose their values consistently with the case discretisation and time stepping.

docs.title: Scaling transferred fluid forces
docs.text:
scaleforce is a child of case/execution/special/chrono, containing body entries selected by mkbound. It is not an attribute to add to bodyfloating. The current format describes its coefficients as scaling the transferred fluid force. For constant coefficients, the component-wise interpretation is

\[F'_x=s_x F_x,\qquad F'_y=s_y F_y,\qquad F'_z=s_z F_z.\]

The following is a single constant-coefficient alternative from the complete Chrono format. Its boundary identifier must correspond to a body declared in the surrounding case. The values are illustrative, not a general prescription for two-dimensional scaling.

XML excerpt — constant-force-scale. XML location: case/execution/special/chrono/scaleforce. Source: doc/xml_format/_FmtXML_Chrono.xml.

<body mkbound="1" x="0.01" y="1" z="1" comment="Scale forces in all directions."/>
Attribute Meaning in this alternative Value mkbound Existing Chrono body's boundary identifier 1 x Factor for the x component 0.01 y Factor for the y component 1 z Factor for the z component 1

The factors are dimensionless. The reader warns when scaleforce is used outside a 2D simulation. Scaling changes the applied loading and therefore the body response; it is not a visualisation setting or a replacement for mass, inertia, material properties, gravity or contact calibration. The reference identifies fluid-force scaling and does not establish a universal rescaling of every contact, constraint, gravitational force or torque.

The complete format also illustrates time-dependent scale entries and an external file. Those are alternatives requiring their own time series and compatible body selection. The current reader's selection of variable series needs confirmation when several body entries coexist; the constant excerpt above does not establish that such combinations are interchangeable or runtime-validated.

docs.title: Collision models and configuration
docs.text: For Chrono contact modelling, check three related parts of the complete case: the CHR collision algorithm, contact/material configuration, and the collision geometry attached to each participating body. Defining a mechanical link alone does not enable body contact.

docs.title: NSC and SMC
Materials and boundary associations
docs.text:
The original illustration identifies a PVC floating cube (mkbound=51) and a steel fixed tank (mkbound=0). The corresponding current case has a floating declaration covering 51–53, while its Chrono collision section declares only cube 51. The range is preserved below; it must not be silently reduced to match the older screenshot.

Figure 1: Fixed steel tank (mkbound=0) and PVC floating body (mkbound=51) used to illustrate the Chrono collision configuration.

XML excerpt — floating-material. XML location: case/casedef. Source: examples/chrono/07_DamBreakCubes/DamBreak1Cube_Def.xml.

<floatings>
    <floating mkbound="51-53" property="pvc">
        <massbody value="2.7"/>
    </floating>
</floatings>

XML excerpt — material-associations. XML location: case/casedef. Source: examples/chrono/07_DamBreakCubes/DamBreak1Cube_Def.xml.

<properties>
    <propertyfile file="Floating_Materials.xml" path="materials"/>
    <links>
        <link mkbound="0" property="steel" comment="Property for the tank"/>
    </links>
</properties>

The named properties come from Floating_Materials.xml, using its materials path. The sibling file in 07_DamBreakCubes contains these values; they are example-specific material settings, not general recommendations:

Quantity XML name Steel PVC Units Young's modulus Young_Modulus/@value 210000000000.0 3000000000.0 N/m² Poisson's ratio PoissonRatio/@value 0.35 0.30 Dimensionless Restitution coefficient Restitution_Coefficient/@value 0.80 0.60 Dimensionless Kinetic friction Kfric/@value 0.35 0.15 Dimensionless

Static friction is an additional v6 consideration absent from the slides' material list. The current loader accepts Sfric; when only one of Kfric and Sfric is provided, it copies that value to the missing coefficient. Thus these source materials, which specify only Kfric, also obtain a static coefficient. Do not invent a separate Sfric value. The format additionally supports Kfric_User, Sfric_User and Restitution_Coefficient_User property overrides.

docs.title: Collision geometry and normals
docs.text:
modelfile="AutoActual" requests generated geometry associated with the body's actual boundary configuration. The current format also documents AutoDp, explicit OBJ/VTK geometry and [CaseName] substitution. Geometry is processed when collisions are active; the absence of a model file leaves that body without an associated contact model in the reference example.

The tank uses modelnormal="invert" so its enclosing surfaces have the intended normal orientation. Inverting the tank is a case-specific choice, not a rule for every fixed body. The original arrows show the distinction between the cube's outer surfaces and the tank's inner contact surfaces.

Figure 2: Contact-surface normals on the floating body and the inner walls of the fixed tank.

For the current IDs, generated filenames follow cube1_mkb0051.obj and tank_mkb0000.obj under chrono_objs/; the older slide uses cube_mkb0051.obj because its body ID differs.

The current reference also includes optional NSC rolling/spinning friction, damping and compliance settings, and SMC kn, gn and adhesion. These are alternatives to extend the appropriate model, not instructions to paste all reference blocks together. The reader rejects inconsistent or duplicate NSC/SMC alternatives. Refer to doc/xml_format/_FmtXML_Chrono.xml for their exact syntax; no numerical tuning or undocumented units are introduced here.

docs.title: Linear spring
docs.text:
link_linearspring connects two body attachment points with stiffness and viscous damping. It is useful for a spring-supported float or a restrained body. The point-absorber source connects fixed Bottom (0) and floating Floater (50), initially separated by 0.325 m. Its floating-body definition permits vertical translation and restricts rotations; the link excerpt alone does not impose those degrees of freedom.

Figure 3: Linear spring connecting the fixed structure and floating body, with an initial attachment-point separation of 0.325 m.

The presentation writes the PTO response as

\[F_{\mathrm{PTO}} = k\,z + c\,\mathrm{vel}.z.\]

Here k and c denote stiffness and viscous damping, and vel.z denotes vertical velocity in the illustrated motion. The slide does not fully specify the zero of z or whether this is a reaction or applied force. The XML specifies a non-zero equilibrium length. Do not substitute the absolute attachment coordinate into this equation or infer a universal force direction from its plus signs.

This is the source's entire chrono element. It still requires its surrounding case and execution/parameters, including the source's collision choice. It is not a standalone executable case.

XML excerpt — linear-spring. XML location: case/execution/special. Source: examples/chrono/10_PointAbsorber/CasePointAbsorberSpring_Def.xml.

<chrono>
    <savedata value="0.05" comment="Saves CSV with data exchange for each time interval (0=all steps)"/>
    <schemescale value="1" comment="Scale used to create the initial scheme of Chrono objects (default=1)"/>
    <bodyfixed id="Bottom" mkbound="0"/>
    <bodyfloating id="Floater" mkbound="50"/>
    <link_linearspring idbody1="Bottom" idbody2="Floater">
        <point_fb1 x="2.0" y="0.0" z="0.0" comment="Point in body 1"/>
        <point_fb2 x="2.0" y="0.0" z="0.325" comment="Point in body 2"/>
        <stiffness value="100.0" comment="Stiffness [N/m]"/>
        <damping value="500.0" comment="Damping [Ns/m]"/>
        <rest_length value="0.325" comment="Spring equilibrium length [m]"/>
        <savevtk>
            <nside value="16" comment="number of sections for each revolution. 0=not saved, 1=line (default=16)"/>
            <radius value="5.0" comment="spring radius (default=3)"/>
            <length value="3.0" comment="length for each revolution (default=1)"/>
        </savevtk>
    </link_linearspring>
</chrono>
Parameter Meaning Units point_fb1, point_fb2 Attachment points associated with body 1 and body 2, supplied at their initial case positions m stiffness/@value Linear stiffness, denoted k in the equation N/m damping/@value Linear viscous damping, denoted c N·s/m rest_length/@value Spring equilibrium length m

For scalar coefficients the XML tags are stiffness and damping, not k and c. The current format also supports time-dependent <k time="..." value="..."> and <c time="..." value="..."> entries within those parents, or external coefficient files. Those alternatives require their own source data and must not be combined with the scalar excerpt indiscriminately.

docs.title: Spring VTK visualisation
docs.text:
savevtk child Meaning in the implementation Units / qualification nside 0: no representation; 1: line; greater than 1: coil Integer selector; source comments describe sections per revolution radius Drawn coil radius factor Scaled by dp × schemescale; not a physical spring radius in metres length Drawn revolution-length factor Scaled by dp × schemescale, with deformation handled by the drawing routine

The coil representation uses a fixed 28 subdivisions per revolution; nside selects whether to draw nothing, a line or a coil. These settings change the drawing, not the spring stiffness or equilibrium length. The CSV interval and VTK output are separate controls.

docs.title: Coulomb damping
docs.text:
link_coulombdamping connects the same pair of attachment points using a Coulomb force parameter. Unlike the viscous term, whose force depends on speed, the illustrated Coulomb response has a specified magnitude opposing the vertical velocity:

\[F_{\mathrm{PTO}} = -\operatorname{sign}(\mathrm{vel}.z)\,F_b.\]

This is the source slide's convention for the illustrated vertical motion. The illustrated expression specifies the force direction for non-zero vertical velocity.

Figure 4: Coulomb damping connection between the fixed structure and floating body, with force opposing vertical motion.

XML excerpt — coulomb-damping. XML location: case/execution/special. Source: examples/chrono/10_PointAbsorber/CasePointAbsorberCoulomb_Def.xml.

<chrono>
    <savedata value="0.05" comment="Saves CSV with data exchange for each time interval (0=all steps)"/>
    <schemescale value="1" comment="Scale used to create the initial scheme of Chrono objects (default=1)"/>
    <bodyfixed id="Bottom" mkbound="0"/>
    <bodyfloating id="Floater" mkbound="50"/>
    <link_coulombdamping idbody1="Bottom" idbody2="Floater">
        <point_fb1 x="2.0" y="0.0" z="0.0" comment="Point in body 1"/>
        <point_fb2 x="2.0" y="0.0" z="0.325" comment="Point in body 2"/>
        <rest_length value="0.325" comment="Spring equilibrium length [m]"/>
        <damping value="10.0" comment="Coulomb force [N]"/>
        <savevtk>
            <nside value="16" comment="number of sections for each revolution. 0=not saved, 1=line (default=16)"/>
            <radius value="5.0" comment="spring radius (default=3)"/>
            <length value="3.0" comment="length for each revolution (default=1)"/>
        </savevtk>
    </link_coulombdamping>
</chrono>
Parameter Meaning Units point_fb1, point_fb2 Initial attachment positions for Bottom and Floater m damping/@value Coulomb force magnitude F_b, here 10.0 N rest_length/@value Equilibrium length retained by this link, here 0.325 m savevtk Same visualisation settings as the linear spring Drawing controls

Despite the shared name damping, its units here are N, not N·s/m. The source floating-body definition again restricts the motion to vertical translation without rotation. Preserve that context when using the complete case.

docs.title: Sliding joint
docs.text:
link_pointline allows its reference point to slide along a specified direction. Rotation depends on the optional rotation vectors. This is useful when a body must follow a straight guide rather than move freely in three dimensions. The slide specifies global directions; the current point-absorber case uses vertical (0,0,1) and a point (2,0,0.4).

Figure 5: Sliding constraint defining the global vertical direction of motion and the joint reference point.

XML excerpt — sliding-joint. XML location: case/execution/special. Source: examples/chrono/10_PointAbsorber/CasePointAbsorberPointLine_Def.xml.

<chrono>
    <savedata value="0.05" comment="Saves CSV with data exchange for each time interval (0=all steps)"/>
    <schemescale value="1" comment="Scale used to create the initial scheme of Chrono objects (default=1)"/>
    <bodyfixed id="Bottom" mkbound="0"/>
    <bodyfloating id="Floater" mkbound="50"/>
    <link_pointline idbody1="Floater">
        <slidingvector x="0" y="0" z="1" comment="Sliding vector direction"/>
        <rotpoint x="2" y="0" z="0.4" comment="Sliding point in the body"/>
        <rotvector x="0" y="0" z="1" comment="Vector direction for rotation, use (0,0,0) for spheric joint (default=(0,0,0))"/>
        <stiffness value="0" comment="Torsional stiffness [Nm/rad]"/>
        <damping value="0" comment="Torsional damping [Nms/rad]"/>
    </link_pointline>
</chrono>
Parameter Meaning Units slidingvector Direction of the permitted sliding line Direction vector rotpoint Initial reference point for the joint m rotvector Optional permitted rotation direction; omitted/zero gives the spherical variant in the reference Direction vector rotvector2 Optional second direction used to prevent the remaining rotation Direction vector; read only when rotvector is present stiffness, damping Torsional coefficients in the documented joint configuration N·m/rad; N·m·s/rad

The source's floating-body translation and rotation DOFs are all enabled; the joint supplies the intended restriction. This differs from the separate spring/Coulomb cases' direct DOF restrictions.

The five current inputs under examples/others/ChronoPointline demonstrate omitted rotation vectors, a rotation axis, a second vector, and multiple point-line links. In the format reference, _rotvector and _rotvector2 are disabled illustrations, not active tags. Active variants use the names without underscores.

docs.title: Spherical joint
docs.text:
link_spheric joins bodies at a shared rotation point while allowing spherical rotation. Omitting idbody2 connects body 1 to the world. Multiple links can form an articulated chain; the torsional stiffness and damping remain properties of each link.

Figure 6: Spherical joints connecting two articulated arms and a terminal body to the fixed reference frame.

The historical diagram shows links at (5,5,5.2), (7,5,5.2) and (9,5,5.2) between arm0 and the world, arm0 and arm1, and arm1 and ball. The current CasePendulum_Def.xml instead defines four arm segments and points along the y direction. Its excerpt below preserves those current coordinates; it does not recreate the diagram's older geometry. Its collision algorithm is FREE, and _savedata is inactive.

XML excerpt — spherical-joint. XML location: case/execution/special. Source: examples/chrono/01_Pendulum/CasePendulum_Def.xml.

<chrono>
    <_savedata value="0.02" comment="Saves CSV with data exchange for each time interval (0=all steps)"/>
    <schemescale value="1" comment="Scale used to create the initial scheme of Chrono objects (default=1)"/>
    <bodyfloating id="arm" mkbound="0-3"/>
    <link_spheric idbody1="arm0">
        <rotpoint x="5" y="5" z="5" comment="Point for rotation"/>
        <stiffness value="0" comment="Torsional stiffness [Nm/rad]"/>
        <damping value="0" comment="Torsional damping [Nms/rad]"/>
    </link_spheric>
    <link_spheric idbody1="arm0" idbody2="arm1">
        <rotpoint x="5" y="6" z="5" comment="Point for rotation"/>
        <stiffness value="0" comment="Torsional stiffness [Nm/rad]"/>
        <damping value="0" comment="Torsional damping [Nms/rad]"/>
    </link_spheric>
    <link_spheric idbody1="arm1" idbody2="arm2">
        <rotpoint x="5" y="7" z="5" comment="Point for rotation"/>
        <stiffness value="0" comment="Torsional stiffness [Nm/rad]"/>
        <damping value="0" comment="Torsional damping [Nms/rad]"/>
    </link_spheric>
    <link_spheric idbody1="arm2" idbody2="arm3">
        <rotpoint x="5" y="8" z="5" comment="Point for rotation"/>
        <stiffness value="0" comment="Torsional stiffness [Nm/rad]"/>
        <damping value="0" comment="Torsional damping [Nms/rad]"/>
    </link_spheric>
</chrono>
Parameter Meaning Units idbody1, idbody2 Connected body IDs; omitted second body means world Body references rotpoint Initial shared rotation point m stiffness/@value Torsional stiffness N·m/rad damping/@value Torsional damping N·m·s/rad

The zero coefficients in this case must not be substituted into other articulated examples as general defaults. See the pendulum catalogue entry for the related family and original videos.

docs.title: Hinge
docs.text:
link_hinge permits rotation around the axis defined by rotpoint and rotvector. With no second body it attaches the wheel to the world. The current wheel case uses the point (1.0,0,0.6) and the y-axis direction (0,1,0).

Figure 8: Hinge joint defining wheel rotation about the specified axis through (1.0, 0.0, 0.6) m.

The presentation gives the torsional response as

\[M_{\mathrm{PTO}} = k\,\theta + c\,\mathrm{vel}.\theta.\]

θ denotes angular displacement and vel.θ angular velocity in the slide's notation. The positive rotation, reference angle and action/reaction interpretation are not fully defined by the slide. The equation is retained without assigning an unsupported universal torque sign.

These are sibling declarations and the hinge from the current wheel-and-pulley case; its pulley link is shown separately below.

XML excerpt — hinge. XML location: case/execution/special/chrono. Source: examples/chrono/11_CurrentWheelPulley/CaseCurrentWheelPulley_Def.xml.

<bodyfixed id="domain" mkbound="0" modelfile="AutoActual"/>
<bodyfloating id="wheel" mkbound="50" modelfile="AutoActual"/>
<bodyfloating id="gear" mkbound="51" modelfile="AutoActual"/>
<link_hinge idbody1="wheel">
    <rotpoint x="1.0" y="0" z="0.6" comment="Point for rotation"/>
    <rotvector x="0.0" y="1.0" z="0.0" comment="Vector direction for rotation"/>
    <stiffness value="0.0" comment="Torsional stiffness [Nm/rad]"/>
    <damping value="0.0" comment="Torsional damping [Nms/rad]"/>
</link_hinge>
Parameter Meaning Units rotpoint Point on the hinge axis m rotvector Axis direction Direction vector stiffness/@value Torsional stiffness k N·m/rad damping/@value Torsional damping c N·m·s/rad

Both coefficients are 0.0 in this wheel case. Non-zero torsional settings occur in other mechanisms, such as the flexible-gate family; retain their own case values rather than borrowing this wheel's zeros.

docs.title: Pulley
docs.text:
link_pulley couples the rotational motion of the wheel and gear using their specified radii. The current source defines a hinge for wheel before the pulley. The reader explicitly checks this relationship and warns when body 1 has no hinge; the pulley excerpt should not be treated as a replacement for that hinge.

Figure 9: Pulley connection between the wheel (mkbound=50, radius 0.3 m) and gear (mkbound=51, radius 0.05 m).

Use the body declarations and hinge from the same source case above. The excerpt retains the current gear-axis coordinates, not the older rounded point in the figure.

XML excerpt — pulley. XML location: case/execution/special/chrono. Source: examples/chrono/11_CurrentWheelPulley/CaseCurrentWheelPulley_Def.xml.

<link_pulley idbody1="wheel" idbody2="gear">
    <rotpoint x="1.0025" y="0" z="1.2025" comment="Point for rotation"/>
    <rotvector x="0.0" y="1.0" z="0.0" comment="Rotation axis of the body"/>
    <radius value="0.3" comment="Radius of idbody1"/>
    <radius2 value="0.05" comment="Radius of idbody2"/>
</link_pulley>
Parameter Meaning Units idbody1, idbody2 Wheel and gear body references IDs; here wheel and gear rotpoint Rotation-axis point supplied for the pulley body m rotvector Rotation-axis direction Direction vector radius/@value Radius of body 1, the wheel m radius2/@value Radius of body 2, the gear m

The source body declarations retain modelfile="AutoActual", but this case has no active collision section. Those attributes alone do not demonstrate enabled contacts.

docs.title: Related documentation and examples
docs.text:
• Coupling DualSPHysics with Project Chrono — coupling theory and background.
  • Chrono Examples Catalogue — all numbered Chrono families, descriptions and videos.
  • Spring examples — spring-linked bodies, including NSC and SMC cases.
  • Project Chrono and its source repository.

For the XML format, see doc/xml_format/_FmtXML_Chrono.xml and doc/xml_format/_FmtXML__Parameters.xml alongside the complete cases cited above. The Chrono format file contains alternative illustrative blocks; it is not a standalone simulation case.

docs.title: Full Chrono XML format reference
docs.text:
The complete Chrono XML format reference is provided below. It documents the configuration structure, available options and supported mechanical constraints. This is a format reference, not a standalone executable simulation case.

doc/xml_format/_FmtXML_Chrono.xml

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" ?>
<!-- *** DualSPHysics [Chrono] v6.0 (16-06-2026) *** -->
<!-- *** class: JChronoObjects *** -->
<!----------------------------------------------------------------------------------->
<!----------------------------------------------------------------------------------->
<!-- *** Example to define the bodies and links using Chrono *** -->
<casedef>
    <!-- Define body materials  -->
    <!-- Floating bodies -->
    <floatings>
        <floating mkbound="1" relativeweight="1.0" property="pvc" comment="Property for the floating bound" />
        <floating mkbound="2" relativeweight="1.2" property="pvc+SetKfric" comment="Property for the floating bound" />
        <floating mkbound="3" relativeweight="1.2" property="pvc+SetSfric" comment="Property for the floating bound" />
        <floating mkbound="4" relativeweight="1.0" property="pvc+SetResCoeff" comment="Property for the floating bound" />
    </floatings>
    <properties>
        <propertyfile file="Floating_Materials.xml" path="materials" />
        <!-- Fixed bodies -->
        <links>
            <link mkbound="0" property="pvc" comment="Property for the fixed bound" />
        </links>
        <!-- The values Kfric_User, Sfric_User and Restitution_Coefficient_User    -->
        <!-- replace to Kfric, Sfric and Restitution_Coefficient values in         -->
        <!-- Floating_Materials.xml -->
        <property name="SetKfric" Kfric_User="0.1234" />
        <property name="SetSfric" Sfric_User="0.1234" />
        <property name="SetResCoeff" Restitution_Coefficient_User="0.4321" />
    </properties>
</casedef>

<!----------------------------------------------------------------------------------->
<!----------------------------------------------------------------------------------->
<!-- *** Special section to define the Chrono's setup *** -->
<execution>
    <special>
        <chrono>
            <savedata value="-1" comment="Saves CSV with data exchange for each time interval (0=all steps)" />
            <schemescale value="1" comment="Scale used to create the initial scheme of Chrono objects (default=1)" />
            <gravity value="true" comment="Use gravity acceleration in Chrono (default=true)" />
            <ompthreads value="1" comment="Number of Chrono OpenMP threads (default=1)" />
            <!-- Optional Chrono internal substepping. -->
            <timestepper>
                <substepping mode="off" comment="off|fixed|auto. When off, one Chrono step is used per DualSPHysics step.">
                    <maxdt value="0" comment="Maximum internal Chrono dt. 0 uses DualSPHysics dt." />
                    <maxsteps value="1" comment="Maximum Chrono substeps per DualSPHysics step." />
                    <maxdispdp value="0" comment="Adaptive limit based on body displacement / dp. 0 disables it." />
                    <maxrot value="0" comment="Adaptive limit based on body rotation [rad]. 0 disables it." />
                </substepping>
            </timestepper>
            <!-- Enable collisions for chrono -->
            <collision activate="true">
                <distancedp value="0.5" comment="Allowed collision overlap according Dp (default=0.5)" />
                <contactmethod value="0" comment="Contact method type. 0:NSC, 1:SMC."/>
            </collision>
            <!-- Disable collisions for chrono -->
            <collision activate="false" />
            <!-- Define the bodies for Chrono -->
            <bodyfixed id="domain" mkbound="0" modelfile="domain.obj" /> <!-- Link a mesh file to enable contact modelling -->
            <bodymoving id="piston" mkbound="10" massbody="10" modelfile="piston.vtk" />
            <bodyfloating id="box1" mkbound="1" modelfile="box.obj" />
            <bodyfloating id="box2" mkbound="2"/> <!-- Don't link a mesh file to disable contact modelling -->
            <bodyfloating id="box3" mkbound="3"/>
            <bodyfloating id="box4" mkbound="4"/>
            <bodyfloating id="box5" mkbound="5"/>
            <!-- Define the restrictions between bodies  -->
            <!-- Spring between two bodies -->
            <link_linearspring idbody1="domain" idbody2="box1">
                <point_fb1 x="1.0" y="1.0" z="1.0" comment="Point in body 1" />
                <point_fb2 x="2.0" y="2.0" z="2.0" comment="Point in body 2" />
                <stiffness value="1000" comment="Stiffness [N/m]" />
                <damping value="100" comment="Damping [Ns/m]" />
                <rest_length value="5.0" comment="Spring equilibrium length [m]" />
                <savevtk>
                    <nside value="16" comment="number of sections for each revolution. 0=not saved, 1=line (default=16)" />
                    <radius value="3" comment="spring radius (default=3)" />
                    <length value="1" comment="length for each revolution (default=1)" />
                </savevtk>
            </link_linearspring>
            <!-- Spring with variable stiffness and damping along time -->
            <link_linearspring idbody1="domain" idbody2="box1">
                <point_fb1 x="1.0" y="1.0" z="1.0" comment="Point in body 1" />
                <point_fb2 x="2.0" y="2.0" z="2.0" comment="Point in body 2" />
                <damping comment="Damping [Ns/m]">     <!--  Variable Damping -->
                    <c time="0" value="0"/>
                    <c time="5" value="0"/>
                    <c time="5" value="500"/>
                    <c time="10" value="500"/>
                </damping>
                <stiffness comment="Stiffness [N/m]"> <!--  Variable Stiffness -->
                    <k time="0" value="0"/>
                    <k time="5" value="0"/>
                    <k time="5" value="100"/>
                    <k time="10" value="100"/>
                </stiffness>
                <rest_length value="5.0" comment="Spring equilibrium length [m]" />
            </link_linearspring>
            <!-- Spring with variable stiffness and damping along time from external file -->
            <link_linearspring idbody1="domain" idbody2="box1">
                <point_fb1 x="1.0" y="1.0" z="1.0" comment="Point in body 1" />
                <point_fb2 x="2.0" y="2.0" z="2.0" comment="Point in body 2" />
                <damping file="CaseExternalDamping.csv" comment="Damping [Ns/m]"/>      <!--  Variable Damping from external file -->   
                <stiffness file="CaseExternalStiffness.csv" comment="Stiffness [N/m]"/> <!--  Variable Stiffness from external file --> 
                <rest_length value="5.0" comment="Spring equilibrium length [m]" />
            </link_linearspring>
            <!-- Coulomb Damping bewteen two bodies -->
            <link_coulombdamping  idbody1="domain" idbody2="box1">
                <point_fb1 x="1.0" y="1.0" z="1.0" comment="Point in body 1" />
                <point_fb2 x="2.0" y="2.0" z="2.0" comment="Point in body 2" />
                <rest_length value="5.0" comment="Spring equilibrium length [m]" />
                <damping value="100" comment="Coulomb force [N]" />
                <savevtk>
                    <nside value="16" comment="number of sections for each revolution. 0=not saved, 1=line (default=16)" />
                    <radius value="3" comment="spring radius (default=3)" />
                    <length value="1" comment="length for each revolution (default=1)" />
                </savevtk>
            </link_coulombdamping>
            <!-- Hinge between two bodies -->
            <link_hinge idbody1="box1" idbody2="box2">
                <rotpoint x="1.0" y="1.0" z="1.0" comment="Point for rotation" />
                <rotvector x="0" y="1" z="0" comment="Vector direction for rotation" />
                <stiffness value="500" comment="Torsional stiffness [Nm/rad]" />
                <damping   value="10" comment="Torsional damping [Nms/rad]" />
            </link_hinge>
            <!-- Spheric joint between two bodies -->
            <link_spheric idbody1="box2" idbody2="box3">
                <rotpoint x="3.0" y="3.0" z="3.0" comment="Point for rotation" />
                <stiffness value="20" comment="Torsional stiffness [Nm/rad]" />
                <damping   value="10" comment="Torsional damping [Nms/rad]" />
            </link_spheric>
            <!-- Define restrictions of a body to absolute space -->
            <!-- Spheric joint or modified joint by rotvector and rotvector2 that can slide along an axis -->
            <link_pointline idbody1="box4">
                <slidingvector x="0" y="1" z="0" comment="Sliding vector direction" />
                <rotpoint x="4.0" y="0" z="4.0" comment="Sliding point in the body" />
                <_rotvector x="0" y="1" z="0" comment="Vector direction for rotation, use (0,0,0) for spheric joint (default=(0,0,0))" />
                <_rotvector2 x="0" y="0" z="1" comment="Second vector to avoid rotation (default=(0,0,0))" />
                <stiffness value="400" comment="Torsional stiffness [Nm/rad]" />
                <damping value="50" comment="Torsional damping [Nms/rad]" />
            </link_pointline>
            <link_pointline idbody1="box4" idbody2="box5">
                <slidingvector x="0" y="1" z="0" comment="Sliding vector direction" />
                <rotpoint x="4.0" y="0" z="4.0" comment="Sliding point in the body" />
                <_rotvector x="0" y="1" z="0" comment="Vector direction for rotation, use (0,0,0) for spheric joint (default=(0,0,0))" />
                <_rotvector2 x="0" y="0" z="1" comment="Second vector to avoid rotation (default=(0,0,0))" />
                <stiffness value="400" comment="Torsional stiffness [Nm/rad]" />
                <damping value="50" comment="Torsional damping [Nms/rad]" />
            </link_pointline>
            <link_spheric idbody1="box5">
                <rotpoint x="5.0" y="5.0" z="5.0" comment="Point for rotation" />
                <stiffness value="20" comment="Torsional stiffness [Nm/rad]" />
                <damping   value="10" comment="Torsional damping [Nms/rad]" />
            </link_spheric>
            <link_pulley idbody1="box1" idbody2="box5">
                <rotpoint x="1.0" y="0" z="1.2" comment="Point for rotation" />
                <rotvector x="0.0" y="1.0" z="0.0" comment="Rotation axis of the body" />
                <radius value="0.3" comment="Radius of idbody1"/>
                <radius2 value="0.05" comment="Radius of idbody2"/>
            </link_pulley>
        </chrono>
    </special>
</execution>

<!----------------------------------------------------------------------------------->
<!----------------------------------------------------------------------------------->
<!-- *** Alternative Chrono collision definitions *** -->
<!-- Use contactmethod value 0 for NSC or value 1 for SMC. -->
<chrono>
    <collision activate="true">
        <distancedp value="0.5" comment="Allowed collision overlap according Dp (default=0.5)" />
        <!--  NSC -->
        <contactmethod value="0" comment="Contact method type. 0:NSC, 1:SMC.">
            <rollingfriction value="0" comment="NSC rolling friction." />
            <spinningfriction value="0" comment="NSC spinning friction." />
            <dampingf value="0" comment="NSC damping factor." />
            <compliance value="0" comment="NSC normal compliance." />
            <compliancet value="0" comment="NSC tangential compliance." />
            <compliancerolling value="0" comment="NSC rolling compliance." />
            <compliancespinning value="0" comment="NSC spinning compliance." />
        </contactmethod>
        <!--  SMC -->
        <contactmethod value="1" comment="Contact method type. 0:NSC, 1:SMC.">
            <kn value="1.0e6" comment="SMC normal stiffness." />
            <gn value="100" comment="SMC normal damping." />
            <adhesion value="0" comment="SMC adhesion." />
        </contactmethod>
    </collision>
</chrono>

<!----------------------------------------------------------------------------------->
<!----------------------------------------------------------------------------------->
<!-- *** Examples of defining the geometry of objects ***                        -->
<!-- Note that geometry definition is only necessary when Chrono manages         -->
<!-- collisions between boundary objects (fixed, moving or floating).            -->
<chrono>
    <savedata value="0.02" comment="Saves CSV with data exchange for each time interval (0=all steps)" />
    <!-- Geometry files (OBJ or VTK files) is defined by "modelfile". -->
    <bodyfloating id="box1" mkbound="1" modelfile="box.obj" />
    <!-- [CaseName] is replaced by case name in DualSPHysics execution. -->
    <bodyfloating id="ball" mkbound="4" modelfile="[CaseName]_WreckingBall_Actual.vtk" />
    <!-- Several objects can be defined in one line using a list of mkbound values. -->
    <!-- The geometry used by each object is according the mk of each object when   -->
    <!-- the VTK file includes information about mk.                                -->
    <bodyfloating id="box" mkbound="51-66,80,82" modelfile="[CaseName]_Boxes_Actual.vtk" />
    <!-- modelfile="AutoActual" or modelfile="AutoDp" can be used to assign the geometry -->
    <!-- automatically from the VTK files generated by GenCase v4.0.074 (or higher).     -->
    <bodyfloating id="box" mkbound="51-66,80,82" modelfile="AutoActual" />
    <!-- The normals of geometry can be changed using modelnormal="invert".          -->
    <!-- The value of modelnormal is "original" by default. The use of "invert" inverts --> 
    <!-- the normal ones. And "twoface" creates normals in both directions but this  --> 
    <!-- option may effect the results of the simulation.                              -->
    <bodyfixed id="domain" mkbound="10" modelfile="AutoActual" modelnormal="invert" />
</chrono>

<!-- ***=============================================================*** -->
<!-- ***=============================================================*** -->
<!-- *** Attribute "scaleforce" in bodyfloating elements to enable   *** -->
<!-- *** the use of a coefficient to scale the forces of each object.*** -->
<!-- *** The scale factor will be multipled by the fluid force       *** -->
<chrono active="true">
    <scaleforce>
        <body mkbound="1" x="0.01" y="1" z="1" comment="Scale forces in all directions."/>
        <body mkbound="2-4" x="0.02" y="1" z="1" comment="Scale forces in all directions."/>
        <body mkbound="5" file="ScaleForce.csv" comment="Scale forces in all directions."/>
        <body mkbound="5" comment="Scale forces in all directions.">
            <scale time="0" x="0.01" y="1" z="1"/>
            <scale time="5" x="0.5" y="1" z="1"/>
            <scale time="5" x="0.8" y="1" z="1"/>
            <scale time="10" x="1" y="1" z="0.5"/>
        </body>
    </scaleforce>
</chrono>

<!-- ***=======================================================================*** -->
<!-- ***=======================================================================*** -->
<!-- *** Attribute "active" in chrono, bodyXXX and link_XXX elements to enable *** -->
<!-- *** (using active="true" or active="1") or disable (using active="false"  *** -->
<!-- *** or active="0"). It is an optional attribute and true by default.      *** -->
<chrono active="true">
    <bodyfixed active="true"/>
    <bodyfloating active="true"/>
    <link_linearspring active="true"/>
    <link_coulombdamping active="true"/>
    <link_hinge active="true"/>
    <link_pointline active="true"/>
    <link_spheric active="true"/>
    <link_pulley active="true"/>
</chrono>

<!-- ***============================================================================*** -->
<!-- ***============================================================================*** -->
<!-- *** Attribute "imposefric" in bodyXXX elements to impose its kfric value when  *** -->
<!-- *** this body collides with other (using imposefric="true" or imposefric="1")  *** --> 
<!-- *** or disable (using imposefric="false" or imposefric="0"). It is an optional *** -->
<!-- *** attribute and false by default.                                            *** -->
<chrono>
    <bodyfixed id="domain" mkbound="10" modelfile="AutoActual" modelnormal="invert" imposefric="true" />
    <bodyfloating id="box" mkbound="51" modelfile="AutoActual" imposefric="true" />
</chrono>

docs.title: ChronoFEA
docs.text:
Under review by Iván Martínez Estévez

Euler–Bernoulli beams, structural nodes and partitioned fluid–structure interaction in DualSPHysics v6.

docs.title: Scope and structural formulation
docs.text:
ChronoFEA couples the SPH fluid solver in DualSPHysics to the finite-element structural solver in Project Chrono through DSPHChronoLib. The structure has two representations: boundary particles provide its interface with the fluid, while a beam mesh supplies its elastic response. Fluid loading deforms the beam; its updated kinematics move the boundary particles for the subsequent fluid interaction. This is a two-way, partitioned SPH–FEA model.

The documented element is a three-dimensional Euler–Bernoulli beam with a corotational formulation, allowing large rotations and displacements while expressing the elastic response in the element frame. Cross-section properties and the beam discretisation govern the structural model. General lists of upstream Chrono capabilities do not imply that shells, cables or solid finite elements can be selected through this interface: the current XML reader accepts beamEuler here.

Rigid-body Chrono describes bodies whose deformation is not resolved, together with mechanical links and contacts. Flexible structures describes the separate Total Lagrangian SPH implementation internal to DualSPHysics. Its flexstrucs material and clamp definitions are not ChronoFEA configuration. These are complementary models with different structural discretisations and XML interfaces.

The coupling requires compatible DualSPHysics, DSPHChronoLib and Chrono libraries with FEA support. A fluid computation on the GPU does not make the Chrono structural solve a GPU finite-element solve. The workshop's compilation examples describe a particular build; use the installation and libraries supplied with the selected release.

Figure 1: Beam centreline and local frames used to describe displacement and orientation in the corotational structural representation.

docs.title: Nodes, segments and section properties
docs.text:
segments specifies the number of beam segments between pointA and pointB. For the documented Euler beam, the number of nodes is

\[N_{\mathrm{nodes}}=N_{\mathrm{segments}}+1.\]

Structural resolution is independent of the SPH particle spacing. Refining the boundary particles alone does not refine the beam mesh. Each endpoint may refer to a shared nodes/node by noderef, or define a unique node directly by coordinates and fixed. A shared reference establishes connectivity; equal coordinates alone should not be treated as an explicit shared-node definition. A fixed node constrains its structural motion; a free node participates in the beam dynamics. Nodal orientation is part of the beam representation as well as nodal position.

Quantity XML Units / meaning Segment count beamEuler/@segments Integer; 64 segments give 65 nodes Circular section section/@shape="0", radius/@value Radius in m Rectangular section section/@shape="1", width, thickness Dimensions in m; Y and Z section directions Structural density density/@value kg/m³; beam material density Young's modulus youngmodulus/@value N/m² Poisson's ratio poisson/@value Dimensionless Damping coefficient rgdamping/@value Rayleigh damping parameter used by the beam model Axial rigidity multiplier axrigmul/@value Dimensionless; default 1; modifies axial rigidity

The current section calculation uses the rectangular second moments and the circular second moment

\[I_y=\frac{b h^3}{12},\qquad I_z=\frac{h b^3}{12},\qquad I_{\mathrm{circle}}=\frac{\pi r^4}{4}.\]

Here \(b\) is section width, \(h\) is section thickness and \(r\) is radius. These describe the section, rather than the fluid smoothing length. rgdamping must not be interpreted as the SPH viscosity or assumed to provide a universal percentage of critical damping. Likewise, an axial multiplier changes structural stiffness and must not be introduced as a harmless formatting adjustment. Supply material properties explicitly rather than borrowing reference-example values.

docs.title: SPH–FEA coupling
docs.text:
The workshop illustrates structural particles grouped into blocks associated with beam nodes. The current implementation also stores each particle's position along a segment and its coordinates in a beam frame. This lets the coupling transfer fluid interaction to the structural discretisation and reconstruct the deformed boundary from the updated beam.

Figure 2: Structural boundary particles grouped into blocks and associated with nodes of the beam representation.

The exchange follows four stages:

  1. DualSPHysics evaluates particle interactions at the fluid–structure interface.
  2. The coupling accumulates structural interaction forces for the beam representation.
  3. Chrono advances the structure, including its material response and configured mechanical restrictions.
  4. Updated nodal positions and orientations determine the boundary deformation; the coupling reconstructs particle motion and evaluates structural deformation and stress information.

For nodal-force transfer, the current implementation distributes a particle's interaction force to the two segment endpoints using its fractional axial coordinate \(\xi_p\):

\[\mathbf f_p=m_p\mathbf a_p^{\mathrm{int}},\qquad \Delta\mathbf F_j=(1-\xi_p)\mathbf f_p,\qquad \Delta\mathbf F_{j+1}=\xi_p\mathbf f_p.\]

The weights are clipped to the interval \([0,1]\). With linearloads enabled, interaction forces are accumulated per segment and divided by the current segment length to obtain distributed loads in N/m. This is a different transfer mode from the nodal-force option; it is not an instruction to divide an external force file by particle spacing.

Figure 3: Particle interaction, structural-force transfer, beam response and reconstruction of the deformed particle boundary, shown from left to right.

userot="true" uses nodal rotations in the reconstruction of the beam frame and bending information. With userot="false", reconstruction uses nodal positions instead. This switch does not redefine the finite-element type or remove all rotational degrees of freedom from the Chrono structural system.

The XML excerpts below are independent selections from their named source. They do not form a newly assembled executable case. Keep the chosen case's geometry, variables, material files, normal vectors and execution settings together.

docs.title: XML organisation
docs.text:
XML location Responsibility case/casedef/geometry Fluid and structural boundary particles, spacing and marker assignment case/casedef/floatings Classifies the structural boundary as floating case/casedef/properties Material associations used where applicable, including contact properties case/casedef/normals Boundary normal definitions for mDBC case/execution/special/chrono/configfea Selects FEA particle objects, output and loading options chrono/nodes Shared structural node definitions chrono/feafloating/beamEuler Beam endpoints, segment count and cross-section properties chrono/link_feahinge Optional FEA-node hinge to the world chrono/collision Contact configuration, separate from structural elasticity case/execution/parameters Fluid, boundary and integration settings of the complete case

The root of the coupling configuration is case/execution/special/chrono. configfea, nodes and feafloating are siblings under chrono; there is no extra chronofea wrapper. The boundary marker in configfea/floating must identify an existing feafloating body and the corresponding particle boundary. It is not the user-defined node reference or the complete particle mk value.

docs.title: Floating classification and structural density
docs.text:
The horizontal-beam case classifies its particle boundary as floating using the following declaration. The beam's physical material density is specified separately in its section. Do not substitute the particle declaration's rhopbody for that section density.

XML excerpt — beam-floating. XML location: case/casedef. Source: examples/chronofea/01_HorizontalBeam/CaseHorizontalBeam_Def.xml. Retain the complete source case and its surrounding definitions.

<floatings>
            <floating mkbound="50" rhopbody="0.1" />
        </floatings>

docs.title: Structural nodes and beam definition
docs.text:
The horizontal beam has two fixed endpoints at (0, 0, −0.025) m and (1, 0, −0.025) m. Its rectangular section is 1 m wide and 0.05 m thick; its density is 2700 kg/m³ and Young's modulus is 67.5 × 10⁹ N/m². The source retains an inactive _size illustration; active rectangular dimensions are width and thickness.

XML excerpt — beam-nodes. XML location: case/execution/special/chrono. Source: examples/chronofea/01_HorizontalBeam/CaseHorizontalBeam_Def.xml. Retain the complete source case and its surrounding definitions.

<nodes>
                    <node ref="0" mass="0" fixed="true" x="0" y="0.0" z="-0.025" comment="Start of beam" />
                    <node ref="1" mass="0" fixed="true" x="1" y="0.0" z="-0.025" comment="End of beam" />
                </nodes>

XML excerpt — horizontal-beam. XML location: case/execution/special/chrono. Source: examples/chronofea/01_HorizontalBeam/CaseHorizontalBeam_Def.xml. Retain the complete source case and its surrounding definitions.

<feafloating id="cylinder1" mkbound="50" massbody="0" type="1" modelfile="AutoActual">
                    <beamEuler segments="64" comment="Number of nodes=Segments+1. Euler beams only use linear order.">
                        <pointA noderef="0" />
                        <pointB noderef="1" />
                        <section shape="1" comment="Shape 0:Circular, 1:Rectangular. (default=0)">
                            <_size x="1.00" y="1.00" z="0.05" comment="Size of the beam sides" />
                            <width value="1.00" comment="Width of the beam (Y-direction)" units_comment="m" />
                            <thickness value="0.05" comment="Thickness of the beam (Z-direction)" units_comment="m" />
                            <density value="2700" comment="Density of the beam." units_comment="kg/m^3" />
                            <poisson value="0.34" comment="Poisson ratio." />
                            <youngmodulus value="67.5E09" comment=" Young elastic modulus." units_comment="N/m^2" />
                            <rgdamping value="0.000" comment="Rayleigh damping ratio." />
                        </section>
                    </beamEuler>
                </feafloating>

The node-count comment above follows the current format. The source case's older Segments+order wording does not introduce an XML order setting. Both fixed endpoints describe this particular supported beam, rather than a free cantilever.

docs.title: Circular sections and unique endpoints
docs.text:
The reference supplies a separate circular-beam alternative. Its 0.03 m radius and 210 × 10⁶ N/m² modulus are illustrative values, not defaults for a steel beam or replacements for the rectangular example.

XML excerpt — circular-beam. XML location: case/execution/special/chrono. Source: doc/xml_format/_FmtXML_ChronoFEA.xml; this is a reference alternative, requiring compatible body and case definitions.

<feafloating id="cylinder1" mkbound="51" modelfile="AutoActual">
                <!-- Define type of FEA Body -->
                <beamEuler segments="10" comment="Number of nodes=Segments+1. Euler beams only use linear order.">
                    <pointA noderef="0" comment="Start of beam"/>
                    <pointB noderef="1" comment="End of beam"/>
                    <!-- Define the section properties -->
                    <!-- Circular beam -->
                    <section shape="0" comment="Shape 0:Circular, 1:Rectangular. (default=0)">
                        <radius value="0.03" comment="Radius of cylinder." units_comment="m"/>
                        <density value="7850" comment="Density of the beam." units_comment="kg/m^3"/>
                        <poisson value="0.3" comment="Poisson ratio."/>
                        <youngmodulus value="210e6" comment=" Young elastic modulus." units_comment="N/m^2"/> 
                        <rgdamping value="0.0" comment="Rayleigh damping ratio."/>
                    </section>
                </beamEuler>
            </feafloating>

An endpoint can instead use fixed, x, y and z directly, as shown in the complete reference. Keep shared noderef endpoints and unique coordinate-defined endpoints distinct. Optional node mass adds a nodal mass in kg; it is separate from section density.

docs.title: FEA output configuration
docs.text:
This is the horizontal-beam case's complete configfea section. Its 0.0001 s CSV interval and precision 16 are case-specific. They are distinct from fluid particle output and the ordinary Chrono exchange CSV interval.

XML excerpt — fea-output. XML location: case/execution/special/chrono. Source: examples/chronofea/01_HorizontalBeam/CaseHorizontalBeam_Def.xml. Retain the complete source case and its surrounding definitions.

<configfea>
                    <savedata value="0.0001" comment="Saves CSV with node positions and node forces (0=all steps)">
                        <start value="0" comment="Start time to save data. (default=0)" />
                        <finish value="10" comment="End time to save data. (default=#TimeMax)" />
                        <precision value="16" comment="Number of digits to save in CSV. (default=6)" />
                    </savedata>
                    <savevtk value="true" comment="Saves vtk with nodes and force points (default=false)" />
                    <floating mkbound="50">
                        <linearloads value="true" comment="Apply linear loads along the beams. (default=false)" />
                    </floating>
                </configfea>
Setting Effect savedata/@value Negative disables periodic FEA CSV; 0 saves every step; positive values specify seconds savedata/start, finish Requested output time window; retain the complete case's simulation duration savedata/precision CSV numerical precision; reader default 6 savevtk Enables both node and geometry VTK output; default false savevtk_nodes Overrides node VTK output; otherwise inherits savevtk savevtk_geo Overrides beam geometry VTK output; otherwise inherits savevtk floating/@userot Uses node rotations in reconstruction; default true

Output paths are relative to the selected simulation output directory. The implementation writes FEA CSV data under fea_data/; node, geometry and force visualisations are managed separately, including FeaVtk/FeaNodes_mkbound_<number>_<sequence>.vtk and node-force products according to enabled outputs. The ordinary Chrono savedata does not replace the FEA output configuration.

docs.title: External nodal forces and distributed loads
docs.text:
loadforces supplies nodal forces in N. loadloads supplies distributed loads in N/m and enables the distributed-load mode. Both require their own external CSV data consistent with the beam discretisation. onlyfile="false" retains the SPH interaction contribution; onlyfile="true" suppresses that contribution for the object. If both loading types are present, an enabled onlyfile on either suppresses SPH loading. This flag should not be interpreted as disabling every independent force in Chrono, such as its configured gravity.

The following are separate reference alternatives for boundary 53. Do not create duplicate configfea/floating entries for one object by concatenating the illustrative alternatives in the complete format.

XML excerpt — external-forces. XML location: case/execution/special/chrono/configfea. Source: doc/xml_format/_FmtXML_ChronoFEA.xml; this is a reference alternative, requiring compatible body and case definitions.

<floating mkbound="53">
                    <loadforces onlyfile="false" file="CaseExternalForces.csv" units_comment="N"/>
                </floating>

XML excerpt — external-loads. XML location: case/execution/special/chrono/configfea. Source: doc/xml_format/_FmtXML_ChronoFEA.xml; independent reference alternative.

<floating mkbound="53">
                    <loadloads onlyfile="false" file="CaseExternalLoads.csv" units_comment="N/m"/>
                </floating>

For SPH distributed loads, use linearloads within the relevant FEA object, as in the horizontal-beam output excerpt. Choose a consistent nodal-force or distributed-load arrangement; do not assume that every combination of nodal-force and distributed-load files has an established physical interpretation.

docs.title: Initial conditions and gravity
docs.text:
Initial linear and angular velocities can be specified per FEA object. The following independent reference alternative uses m/s and rad/s respectively; it requires an existing body 55.

XML excerpt — initial-velocities. XML location: case/execution/special/chrono/configfea. Source: doc/xml_format/_FmtXML_ChronoFEA.xml; this is a reference alternative, requiring compatible body and case definitions.

<floating mkbound="55">
                    <linearvelini x="1" y="3" z="2" units_comment="m/s" />
                    <angularvelini x="0.2" y="0.4" z="0.6" units_comment="rad/s" />
                </floating>

The shared chrono/gravity setting controls Chrono gravity; the FEA reference describes it as distributed loading along beam segments. Preserve the selected case's gravity and initial conditions rather than adding values from this alternative.

docs.title: FEA-node hinge
docs.text:
link_feahinge connects a referenced FEA node to a hinge fixed in space. This is a different declaration from the rigid-body link_hinge. noderef identifies an existing structural node, and idbody1 identifies the FEA body. The optional rotpoint is a global point; when omitted, the current reader uses the initial node position. rotvector is the global hinge axis.

XML excerpt — fea-hinge. XML location: case/execution/special/chrono. Source: doc/xml_format/_FmtXML_ChronoFEA.xml; this is a reference alternative, requiring compatible body and case definitions.

<link_feahinge idbody1="cylinder1" noderef="0">
                <rotpoint x="0" y="0" z="0" comment="Point for rotation in global coordinates (optional)" />
                <rotvector x="0" y="0" z="1" comment="Hinge axis in global coordinates" />
                <rotstiffness value="500" comment="Rotational stiffness around hinge axis [Nm/rad]" />
                <rotdamping value="10" comment="Rotational damping around hinge axis [Nms/rad]" />
            </link_feahinge>

Here rotstiffness=500 has units N·m/rad and rotdamping=10 has units N·m·s/rad. These names must not be replaced by the rigid-hinge stiffness and damping tags. Ensure the chosen node's fixed/free definition is consistent with its intended hinge; do not also fix all its motion and expect a freely rotating support.

docs.title: Contact alternatives
docs.text:
The current FEA format requires SMC when FEA collisions are enabled. The ordinary rigid-body NSC alternative is not a valid substitute. Contacts also require compatible collision geometry and material definitions; modelfile="AutoActual" alone does not enable them.

XML excerpt — fea-collision. XML location: case/execution/special. Source: doc/xml_format/_FmtXML_ChronoFEA.xml; this is a reference alternative, requiring compatible body and case definitions.

<chrono>
    <collision activate="true">
        <distancedp value="0.5" comment="Allowed collision overlap according Dp (default=0.5)" />
        <contactmethod value="1" comment="Contact method type. 0:NSC, 1:SMC. SMC is required for FEA collisions.">
            <kn value="1.0e6" comment="SMC normal stiffness." />
            <gn value="100" comment="SMC normal damping." />
            <adhesion value="0" comment="SMC adhesion." />
        </contactmethod>
        <feacollision mode="mesh-rigidbody" overlap="0"
            comment="mode=mesh-rigidbody|mesh-mesh. overlap=0 uses beam radius/half-size as node-cloud contact radius." />
    </collision>
</chrono>

feacollision/@mode selects mesh-rigidbody or mesh-mesh. overlap must be non-negative; the format specifies that 0 uses the beam radius or half-size for the node-cloud contact radius. The three numbered FEA cases cited here disable collisions. Their fluid–structure interaction therefore does not validate either contact alternative. The contact coefficients shown above are reference examples, not calibrated values for arbitrary materials.

docs.title: Horizontal beam
docs.text: examples/chronofea/01_HorizontalBeam/CaseHorizontalBeam_Def.xml provides the fixed-end beam shown in the excerpts above, using 64 segments, mDBC and the source's fluid/numerical configuration. Its linearloads choice transfers distributed loads. The source also contains historical timestepper value="0" alpha="-0.3" attributes; these must not be used to infer a supported HHT selector in current v6. The current reader selects its implicit Euler setting and reads the documented nested substepping controls. See Chrono time controls.

docs.title: Flexible gate
docs.text:
examples/chronofea/02_FlexibleGate/CaseFlexibleGate_Def.xml describes a 0.079 m gate of thickness 0.005 m. The lower endpoint is free and the upper endpoint fixed; its 40 segments give 41 nodes. Its variables, geometry and inlet/outlet configuration remain part of the complete case.

XML excerpt — gate-nodes. XML location: case/execution/special/chrono. Source: examples/chronofea/02_FlexibleGate/CaseFlexibleGate_Def.xml. Retain the complete source case and its surrounding definitions.

<nodes>
                    <node ref="0" mass="0" fixed="false" x="0.1025" y="0.0" z="#baseOffset" comment="Start of beam"/>
                    <node ref="1" mass="0" fixed="true" x="0.1025" y="0.0" z="#beamLength+baseOffset" comment="End of beam"/>
                </nodes>

XML excerpt — gate-beam. XML location: case/execution/special/chrono. Source: examples/chronofea/02_FlexibleGate/CaseFlexibleGate_Def.xml. Retain the complete source case and its surrounding definitions.

<feafloating id="cylinder1" mkbound="50" massbody="0" type="1" modelfile="AutoActual">
                    <beamEuler segments="40" comment="Number of nodes=Segments+1. Euler beams only use linear order.">
                        <pointA noderef="0"/>
                        <pointB noderef="1"/>
                        <section shape="1" comment="Shape 0:Circular, 1:Rectangular. (default=0)">
                          <_size x="#tbeam" y="1" z="#beamLength" comment="Size of the beam sides"/>

docs.title: Limitations and related documentation
docs.text:
This guide covers the currently documented Euler beam interface. A beam idealisation needs a suitable structural geometry and resolution; it does not establish a general three-dimensional solid constitutive model. Large rotation support does not remove the assumptions of Euler–Bernoulli theory. Contacts, external loads, hinges and substepping need a compatible complete configuration and appropriate numerical validation.

  • Chrono rigid-body XML Guide, including shared collision and time controls and the complete Chrono format.
  • TL-SPH Flexible Structures, for the independent particle-based structural formulation.
  • ChronoFEA Examples Catalogue, for the three numbered families and their original videos.
  • mDBC XML Guide, for boundary normals and slip treatment.
